title: Moscow Court Issues Arrest Warrant for Zhanna Nemtsova
text: Moscow Court Issues Arrest Warrant for Zhanna Nemtsova Sep. 17, 2026 Zhanna Nemtsova. MSC / Kuhlmann (CC BY 3.0 de) A Moscow judge has issued an arrest warrant for Zhanna Nemtsova, the daughter of the late Kremlin critic Boris Nemtsov, state-run media reported Thursday. The warrant went into effect after a judge at the Moscow City Court upheld Nemtsova’s earlier pre-trial detention in absentia, which a lower court issued on July 31. “An arrest warrant has been issued for Nemtsova Zhanna Borisovna,” the state-run RIA Novosti news agency quoted the judge as saying as she rejected the defense’s appeal. Nemtsova, who has lived in Europe for several years, faces charges of organizing the activities of an “undesirable” organization. title: Two-Time Olympic Biathlon Champion and State Duma Lawmaker Sergei Tchepikov Dies at 59
text: Two-Time Olympic Biathlon Champion and State Duma Lawmaker Sergei Tchepikov Dies at 59 Sep. 17, 2026 Sergei Tchepikov. Video grab Two-time Olympic biathlon champion and State Duma lawmaker Sergei Tchepikov has died at age 59, the Russian Biathlon Union said Thursday. The cause of Tchepikov’s death was not disclosed, but unverified reporting by a Telegram channel with links to Russian law enforcement claimed he died of cancer at the hospital. During his international career spanning two decades and six Winter Olympic Games, Tchepikov won a gold medal in the biathlon relay in 1988 and another in the sprint in 1994. Tchepikov was also a two-time World Champion, taking gold in the team event in 1989 and the mixed relay in 2006, with a less successful career in cross-country skiing in between. In 2006, he joined the ruling United Russia party, which is backed by President Vladimir Putin, and was elected to the Sverdlovsk region’s legislative assembly in 2011. He has served in the Duma since 2016. The United States, the EU and other Western countries sanctioned Tchepikov in 2022 for voting in support of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. text: Raiffeisen Bank Helping Russia Circumvent Sanctions, Report Claims By Reuters Sep. 17, 2026 The Raiffeisen Bank branch in Moscow. Shakko (CC BY-SA 4.0) Austria's Raiffeisen Bank International ( RBI ) is facing renewed scrutiny as the biggest Western bank still operating in Russia, after a short-selling firm alleged it was a key channel enabling more than $1 billion of Russian trade to circumvent sanctions. On Thursday, Raiffeisen said the report published by Grizzly Research was misleading and contained factual errors. Raiffeisen's bank in Russia is the biggest lender in the country not subject to sanctions, which have isolated local rivals, meaning it has become crucial for trade payments, including gas exports to Europe. Grizzly Research claimed the bank had become a "key channel" for getting around Western sanctions against Russia, involving trade of more than $1 billion and including some goods used in Russian weapons . title: Russia and Ukraine Exchange Bodies of 275 Fallen Soldiers
text: Russia and Ukraine Exchange Bodies of 275 Fallen Soldiers Sep. 17, 2026 BELTA Russia and Ukraine exchanged the remains of 275 soldiers killed during the war , officials and Belarusian state media reported Thursday. The exchange took place at the Novaya Guta border crossing point in Belarus, Shamsail Saraliyev, a State Duma lawmaker from the ruling United Russia party and member of a parliamentary group dedicated to the conflict, told the RBC news outlet. Russia handed over 252 bodies to Ukrainian authorities, while Ukraine returned 23 bodies. “Belarus continues its humanitarian mission,” the country’s state news agency Belta said in a report that included photos of the exchange. The Ukrainian military confirmed the swap and credited its search teams for continuing their work “despite the threat of drone strikes, remote mining and enemy shelling.” Ukraine’s Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War said law enforcement agencies will work to identify the 252 returned bodies. title: Bear Kills 2 Berry Pickers in Siberia’s Irkutsk Region
text: Bear Kills 2 Berry Pickers in Siberia’s Irkutsk Region Sep. 17, 2026 A bear staring ominously in the distance. John Thomas / unsplash A bear killed two men who were gathering wild berries in Siberia’s Irkutsk region, police said Thursday, coming amid a reported rise in deadly encounters between humans and bears since the spring. Law enforcement said the bear attacked three people who were foraging in the Taiga, killing a 55-year-old and a 65-year-old on Wednesday in a remote forest on the banks of the Lena River, located around 4,200 kilometers (2,610 miles) east of Moscow. “One person managed to escape and report the incident,” the regional branch of Russia’s Interior Ministry said. A search team of police officers and hunters located the bodies of the two men in the forest and opened fire after the bear was said to have appeared and behaved aggressively. The bear fled the area, and authorities are trying to track it down. At least 14 people are now reported to have been killed in bear attacks across Russia since the start of the year, according to a tally by The Moscow Times. text: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Yaroslavl Oil Refinery Sep. 17, 2026 Smoke rising from the Slavneft-Yanos refinery following a drone strike on Sept. 17, 2026. @supernova_plus / Telegram An overnight Ukrainian drone attack sparked a fire at one of Russia’s largest oil refineries in the city of Yaroslavl northeast of Moscow, Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Yevrayev said Thursday. “There’s damage to the oil refinery,” Yevrayev wrote in a post on Telegram, referring to the Slavneft-Yanos refinery, which is jointly controlled by Rosneft and Gazprom. Ukraine’s military has previously claimed attacks on Slavneft-Yanos, saying it provides fuel and lubricants for the Russian military. Slavneft-Yanos has a crude processing capacity of 300,000 barrels per day, or 15 million metric tons per year. Governor Yevrayev reported no casualties and said the refinery fire was fully extinguished by Thursday morning. title: U.S. Congress Passes ‘Sanctions From Hell’ Bill Against Russia
text: U.S. Congress Passes ‘Sanctions From Hell’ Bill Against Russia By Reuters Sep. 17, 2026 nationalaffairs.com The U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday passed a sweeping sanctions and tariff bill intended to increase economic pressure on Russia over its invasion of Ukraine, sending the bill to U.S. President Donald Trump to sign into law more than a year after the late Senator Lindsey Graham first introduced it. The bill, now called the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026" to honor the South Carolina Republican, passed the Senate last month. The House passed it by 262 to 159, as 58 Democrats broke with party leaders to join all but seven Republicans in favor. The legislation targets Russia 's energy and defense industries, as well as its "shadow fleet" of tankers that evade existing sanctions, in order to deprive Moscow of funds used to pay for its war against Ukraine. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Thursday that further U.S. sanctions against Russia would make it harder to reach a peace deal in Ukraine. title: Command disbands Operation Task Force East
text: News , Units – September 17, 2026 Command disbands Operation Task Force East Jerome Rendall Share: The command of the Defense Forces has decided to disband Operational Task Force East, according to two sources close to Hromadske . The news comes shortly after it was reported that the Commander-in-Chief had decided to establish two new groupings of troops — Operational Task Force Azov and Operational Task Force Center. The two new task forces will divide the area of responsibility previously assigned to Operational Task Force East. Read also Defense Forces Establish Two New Operation Task Forces in Donetsk Oblast Major General Viktor Nikolyuk has already confirmed that he is leaving his position as commander Operational Task Force East. Nikolyuk announced his departure on Facebook. However, he remains in the position of the commander of Operational Command East, according to TSN journalist Yuila Kirienko . Nikolyuk was appointed commander in April 2026, replacing Brigadier General Dmytro Bratishko. Before that, he commanded Operational Tactical Group Donetsk and later the 20th Army Corps. title: Two-Time Olympic Biathlon Champion and State Duma Lawmaker Sergei Tchepikov Dies at 59
text: Two-Time Olympic Biathlon Champion and State Duma Lawmaker Sergei Tchepikov Dies at 59 Sep. 17, 2026 Sergei Tchepikov. Video grab Two-time Olympic biathlon champion and State Duma lawmaker Sergei Tchepikov has died at age 59, the Russian Biathlon Union said Thursday. The cause of Tchepikov’s death was not disclosed, but unverified reporting by a Telegram channel with links to Russian law enforcement claimed he died of cancer at the hospital. During his international career spanning two decades and six Winter Olympic Games, Tchepikov won a gold medal in the biathlon relay in 1988 and another in the sprint in 1994. Tchepikov was also a two-time World Champion, taking gold in the team event in 1989 and the mixed relay in 2006, with a less successful career in cross-country skiing in between. In 2006, he joined the ruling United Russia party, which is backed by President Vladimir Putin, and was elected to the Sverdlovsk region’s legislative assembly in 2011. He has served in the Duma since 2016. The United States, the EU and other Western countries sanctioned Tchepikov in 2022 for voting in support of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. title: Command disbands Operation Task Force East
text: News , Units – September 17, 2026 Command disbands Operation Task Force East Jerome Rendall Share: The command of the Defense Forces has decided to disband Operational Task Force East, according to two sources close to Hromadske . The news comes shortly after it was reported that the Commander-in-Chief had decided to establish two new groupings of troops — Operational Task Force Azov and Operational Task Force Center. The two new task forces will divide the area of responsibility previously assigned to Operational Task Force East. Read also Defense Forces Establish Two New Operation Task Forces in Donetsk Oblast Major General Viktor Nikolyuk has already confirmed that he is leaving his position as commander Operational Task Force East. Nikolyuk announced his departure on Facebook. However, he remains in the position of the commander of Operational Command East, according to TSN journalist Yuila Kirienko . Nikolyuk was appointed commander in April 2026, replacing Brigadier General Dmytro Bratishko. Before that, he commanded Operational Tactical Group Donetsk and later the 20th Army Corps. Tchepikov was also a two-time World Champion, taking gold in the team event in 1989 and the mixed relay in 2006, with a less successful career in cross-country skiing in between. In 2006, he joined the ruling United Russia party, which is backed by President Vladimir Putin, and was elected to the Sverdlovsk region’s legislative assembly in 2011. He has served in the Duma since 2016. The United States, the EU and other Western countries sanctioned Tchepikov in 2022 for voting in support of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. text: Raiffeisen Bank Helping Russia Circumvent Sanctions, Report Claims By Reuters Sep. 17, 2026 The Raiffeisen Bank branch in Moscow. Shakko (CC BY-SA 4.0) Austria's Raiffeisen Bank International ( RBI ) is facing renewed scrutiny as the biggest Western bank still operating in Russia, after a short-selling firm alleged it was a key channel enabling more than $1 billion of Russian trade to circumvent sanctions. On Thursday, Raiffeisen said the report published by Grizzly Research was misleading and contained factual errors. Raiffeisen's bank in Russia is the biggest lender in the country not subject to sanctions, which have isolated local rivals, meaning it has become crucial for trade payments, including gas exports to Europe. Grizzly Research claimed the bank had become a "key channel" for getting around Western sanctions against Russia, involving trade of more than $1 billion and including some goods used in Russian weapons . "We stand by the strength of our compliance systems, which have been reviewed many times," Raiffeisen said on Thursday. title: Russia and Ukraine Exchange Bodies of 275 Fallen Soldiers
text: Russia and Ukraine Exchange Bodies of 275 Fallen Soldiers Sep. 17, 2026 BELTA Russia and Ukraine exchanged the remains of 275 soldiers killed during the war , officials and Belarusian state media reported Thursday. The exchange took place at the Novaya Guta border crossing point in Belarus, Shamsail Saraliyev, a State Duma lawmaker from the ruling United Russia party and member of a parliamentary group dedicated to the conflict, told the RBC news outlet. Russia handed over 252 bodies to Ukrainian authorities, while Ukraine returned 23 bodies. “Belarus continues its humanitarian mission,” the country’s state news agency Belta said in a report that included photos of the exchange. The Ukrainian military confirmed the swap and credited its search teams for continuing their work “despite the threat of drone strikes, remote mining and enemy shelling.” Ukraine’s Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War said law enforcement agencies will work to identify the 252 returned bodies. title: Bear Kills 2 Berry Pickers in Siberia’s Irkutsk Region
text: Bear Kills 2 Berry Pickers in Siberia’s Irkutsk Region Sep. 17, 2026 A bear staring ominously in the distance. John Thomas / unsplash A bear killed two men who were gathering wild berries in Siberia’s Irkutsk region, police said Thursday, coming amid a reported rise in deadly encounters between humans and bears since the spring. Law enforcement said the bear attacked three people who were foraging in the Taiga, killing a 55-year-old and a 65-year-old on Wednesday in a remote forest on the banks of the Lena River, located around 4,200 kilometers (2,610 miles) east of Moscow. “One person managed to escape and report the incident,” the regional branch of Russia’s Interior Ministry said. A search team of police officers and hunters located the bodies of the two men in the forest and opened fire after the bear was said to have appeared and behaved aggressively. The bear fled the area, and authorities are trying to track it down. At least 14 people are now reported to have been killed in bear attacks across Russia since the start of the year, according to a tally by The Moscow Times. title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Yaroslavl Oil Refinery
text: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Yaroslavl Oil Refinery Sep. 17, 2026 Smoke rising from the Slavneft-Yanos refinery following a drone strike on Sept. 17, 2026. @supernova_plus / Telegram An overnight Ukrainian drone attack sparked a fire at one of Russia’s largest oil refineries in the city of Yaroslavl northeast of Moscow, Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Yevrayev said Thursday. “There’s damage to the oil refinery,” Yevrayev wrote in a post on Telegram, referring to the Slavneft-Yanos refinery, which is jointly controlled by Rosneft and Gazprom. Ukraine’s military has previously claimed attacks on Slavneft-Yanos, saying it provides fuel and lubricants for the Russian military. Slavneft-Yanos has a crude processing capacity of 300,000 barrels per day, or 15 million metric tons per year. Governor Yevrayev reported no casualties and said the refinery fire was fully extinguished by Thursday morning. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the strike on Slavneft-Yanos and reported damage to three Russian transport aircraft and three helicopters in a separate attack on a military airfield in the southern Rostov region. title: U.S. Congress Passes ‘Sanctions From Hell’ Bill Against Russia
text: U.S. Congress Passes ‘Sanctions From Hell’ Bill Against Russia By Reuters Sep. 17, 2026 nationalaffairs.com The U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday passed a sweeping sanctions and tariff bill intended to increase economic pressure on Russia over its invasion of Ukraine, sending the bill to U.S. President Donald Trump to sign into law more than a year after the late Senator Lindsey Graham first introduced it. The bill, now called the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026" to honor the South Carolina Republican, passed the Senate last month. The House passed it by 262 to 159, as 58 Democrats broke with party leaders to join all but seven Republicans in favor. The legislation targets Russia 's energy and defense industries, as well as its "shadow fleet" of tankers that evade existing sanctions, in order to deprive Moscow of funds used to pay for its war against Ukraine. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Thursday that further U.S. sanctions against Russia would make it harder to reach a peace deal in Ukraine.
